tips.title: Neighboring Tabs = Better Suggestions
tips.content: Copilot uses your open editor tabs as implicit context. Keep related files open — your interfaces, tests, and config files all feed the model. The more relevant context visible, the sharper the completions.

tips.title: High-Level Context Comment
tips.content: Start every new file with a comment describing its purpose, stack, and constraints. 'Express REST API for order fulfillment, Node.js 22, Zod validation' gives Copilot a blueprint for every suggestion in that file.

tips.title: Examples Drive Patterns
tips.content: Write 2–3 examples of the pattern you want before letting Copilot continue. Function signatures, data shapes, and naming styles all teach Copilot what 'good' looks like in your codebase.

tips.title: Slash Commands Cheat Sheet
tips.content: Essential slash commands: /explain (understand code), /fix (debug errors), /tests (generate tests), /doc (add documentation), /new (scaffold a file), /init (configure your project for AI with custom instructions). Type / in the Chat input to see the full list.

tips.title: Keyboard Shortcuts You Need
tips.content: Completions: Tab=accept, Esc=dismiss, Alt+]/ Alt+[=cycle suggestions, Ctrl+Enter=open suggestion panel. Chat: Ctrl+Alt+I (Win/Linux) or Ctrl+Cmd+I (Mac)=Chat view, Ctrl+I=Inline chat, Ctrl+Shift+Alt+L=Quick Chat popup.

tips.title: Public Code Duplication Filter
tips.content: Copilot's duplication filter detects and suppresses completions that match public code verbatim. This reduces the risk of inadvertently introducing GPL or MIT code you did not intend to use.

tips.title: Test-Driven Development with Copilot
tips.content: Write the test name and its describe/it blocks first, then let Copilot generate both the test body and the implementation to make it pass. TDD turns Copilot into a spec-driven code generator.

tips.title: Inline Chat for Surgical Edits
tips.content: Press Ctrl+I (Cmd+I on Mac) to open a chat prompt directly inside the editor. Select code first for targeted refactors. Changes appear as inline diffs you accept or reject — no context switching required.

tips.title: # and @ Context Variables
tips.content: Type # in the chat input to attach explicit context: #file (a specific file), #codebase (semantic search across all files), #terminalSelection (last terminal output), #fetch (live URL content). Use @ to invoke participants: @vscode (IDE questions), @terminal (shell help).

tips.title: Fix Errors Directly from the Terminal
tips.content: When a command fails in the VS Code integrated terminal, click the sparkle icon or 'Fix with Copilot' button that appears in the terminal toolbar. Copilot reads the error output and proposes a corrective action.

tips.title: Meaningful Names = Better Completions
tips.content: Descriptive names are free tokens. 'calculateCompoundInterestMonthly' tells Copilot the algorithm, domain, and time unit. Abbreviations like 'calcCI' force the model to guess — and it sometimes guesses wrong.

tips.title: Copilot in the Terminal (gh CLI)
tips.content: Run 'gh extension install github/gh-copilot' to bring Copilot into your shell. Use 'gh copilot suggest "create a docker network"' to get runnable shell commands, and 'gh copilot explain "git rebase -i HEAD~3"' to demystify any command.

tips.title: AI-Generated PR Descriptions
tips.content: In VS Code with the GitHub Pull Requests extension, use the Copilot sparkle button in the PR description field to auto-generate a clear, structured summary of your changes — saves minutes on every PR.

tips.title: Regex from Plain English
tips.content: Describe your pattern in a comment: '// match ISO 8601 dates with optional time zone offset'. Copilot's regex generation is one of its strongest skills — far faster than trial-and-error on regex101.com.

tips.title: Complex SQL from Natural Language
tips.content: Comment the shape of the result you need: '// monthly revenue by region, last 12 months, exclude test accounts'. Copilot handles window functions, CTEs, and multi-table joins reliably when you describe the output.

tips.title: Agent Mode: Your Autonomous Dev Partner
tips.content: Agent mode (VS Code 1.99+) lets Copilot plan, edit multiple files, run terminal commands, and self-correct — all in one session. Open Chat (Ctrl+Alt+I), select 'Agent' from the agent picker, and describe a full feature. The agent loop handles the rest.

tips.title: Documentation Generation
tips.content: Type '/**' above any function to trigger JSDoc/docstring generation, or use /doc in chat after selecting a function. Copilot infers parameter types, return values, and edge cases from the implementation — not just the signature.

tips.title: Paste Error Messages as Context
tips.content: Copy a stack trace or compiler error into the chat prompt before describing your question. Copilot uses the exact error text to pinpoint root cause. More specific error context = fewer back-and-forth turns.

tips.title: Multi-File Edits with Agent Mode
tips.content: In agent mode, Copilot edits files across your entire project autonomously. It reads relevant files, applies coordinated changes, and presents inline diffs for each file. Use 'Keep' or 'Undo' per file, or roll back via chat checkpoints.

tips.title: .copilotignore for Sensitive Files
tips.content: Create a .copilotignore file (gitignore syntax) to prevent Copilot from reading secrets, PII datasets, or proprietary configs. Place it in the repo root. Enterprise admins can also enforce exclusions at the org level via policy settings on GitHub.com.

tips.title: Cross-Language Code Translation
tips.content: Paste a function and write: 'Translate this Python to TypeScript, preserving the same error handling approach.' Copilot handles idiomatic conversion — not just syntax mapping — including framework-equivalent patterns.

tips.title: AI Commit Messages
tips.content: Stage your changes in VS Code's Source Control panel and click the sparkle (✨) icon in the commit message box. Copilot reads the diff and writes a Conventional Commits-formatted message in seconds.

tips.title: API Client from OpenAPI Specs
tips.content: Paste an OpenAPI/Swagger spec or endpoint documentation block into chat and ask Copilot to generate a typed API client. It produces proper types, error handling, and retry logic — not just raw fetch calls.

tips.title: Realistic Mock Data on Demand
tips.content: Describe the shape you need in a comment: '// 20 employee records with realistic names, departments, hire dates, and salaries'. Copilot generates seeded test data that matches your schema — perfect for tests and demos.

tips.title: Public Code Filter = License Safety
tips.content: Copilot's public code filter detects verbatim matches against its training set and suppresses them. For extra protection, enable 'block suggestions matching public code' in GitHub Copilot settings on GitHub.com.

tips.title: Next Edit Suggestions (NES)
tips.content: Next Edit Suggestions predicts your next logical edit based on what you just changed. When NES has a suggestion, a gray arrow appears in the gutter — press Tab to jump to and accept the next predicted change. Great for rename cascades and repetitive edits.

tips.title: Knowledge Bases for Enterprise Context
tips.content: Copilot Enterprise users can attach knowledge bases built from internal wikis, architecture docs, or runbooks. When attached, Copilot answers questions using your organization's own documentation — not just public knowledge.

tips.title: Auto Model Selection
tips.content: Select 'Auto' from the model picker in the Chat view and VS Code automatically routes each request to the best available model (currently chooses among Claude Sonnet 4, GPT-5, GPT-5 mini). Reduces rate-limit headaches on heavy days.

tips.title: Build Custom Agents
tips.content: Create a custom agent by adding an .agent.md file to .github/agents/. Define the agent's persona, tools, and instructions. Your agent appears in the Chat agent picker alongside the built-in Agent, Plan, and Ask agents.

tips.title: Responsible AI: You Are the Reviewer
tips.content: Copilot is a probability engine, not an oracle. Always review generated code for logic errors, security vulnerabilities, and license issues before committing. OWASP Top 10 still applies to AI-generated code.

tips.title: Word-by-Word Acceptance
tips.content: Press Ctrl+Right Arrow (Cmd+Right on Mac) to accept a completion one word at a time. Useful when a suggestion is mostly right but ends with something you want to rephrase.

tips.title: Enterprise Content Exclusions
tips.content: Copilot Business/Enterprise admins can exclude specific repositories, file paths, or file types from being used as context in completions. Configured via the Copilot policy settings on GitHub.com — no client config required.

tips.title: Configurable Thinking Effort
tips.content: Reasoning models (Claude Sonnet, o3, etc.) let you set thinking effort. In the model picker, click the '>' arrow next to a reasoning model to choose Low, Medium, or High. Use High for complex architecture decisions; Low for quick boilerplate generation.

tips.title: Edge Case Test Generation
tips.content: Ask Copilot: 'Generate tests for null inputs, empty arrays, max integer values, and concurrent calls.' Specifying edge case categories explicitly produces far better coverage than 'write tests for this function'.

tips.title: #codebase Semantic Search
tips.content: Use #codebase in a chat prompt to trigger semantic search across your entire project: 'Where is JWT validation handled? #codebase'. Copilot reads and synthesizes across files — no grep required.

tips.title: MCP Servers Extend Copilot's Reach
tips.content: Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers give Copilot access to live data. Configure them in .vscode/mcp.json. Popular MCP servers cover GitHub, Postgres, Jira, file systems, and REST APIs. Copilot agents can then call these tools mid-task.

tips.title: Reusable Prompt Files
tips.content: Create .prompt.md files in .github/prompts/ to define reusable slash commands for your team. Add a YAML frontmatter 'description' field and invoke with /your-prompt-name in chat. Great for code review checklists, PR templates, and release scripts.

tips.title: Custom Instructions for Your Project
tips.content: Create .github/copilot-instructions.md to define project-wide coding standards, naming conventions, and preferred libraries. Copilot applies these instructions automatically to every chat request in that workspace — no need to repeat yourself in every prompt.

tips.title: Agent Toolsets
tips.content: Configure toolsets in VS Code settings (chat.toolsets) to give agents access to specific terminal commands, build scripts, and linters. Toolsets are reusable across sessions and let you control exactly what an agent can run.

tips.title: Manage Multiple Agent Sessions
tips.content: Open the Sessions view in the Chat panel to run parallel agent sessions — one refactoring a module, another writing tests, a third updating docs. Each session is independent with its own history, file changes, and checkpoints.

tips.title: Plan Agent: Think Before You Build
tips.content: Select 'Plan' from the agent picker to create a structured implementation plan before any code is written. The Plan agent analyzes your codebase, asks clarifying questions, and produces a step-by-step spec. Hand it off to Agent mode to execute when ready.

tips.title: Chat Checkpoints and Rollback
tips.content: VS Code automatically creates checkpoints at key points in an agent session. If a change goes sideways, open the session history, find a prior checkpoint, and restore to that state — like undo but for entire multi-file edits.

tips.title: Multi-Model Selection
tips.content: Use the model picker in the Chat input to choose the right model for the job: fast models (GPT-4.1, Claude Haiku) for quick edits and Q&A; reasoning models (o3, Claude Sonnet 4.6) for complex refactoring or architecture. Premium requests have a cost multiplier shown in the picker.

tips.title: #fetch Live Web Content
tips.content: Use #fetch in a chat prompt to pull live content from a URL into your conversation: 'Summarize the breaking changes in this release notes page: #fetch https://example.com/changelog'. Copilot reads the page and responds with full context.

tips.title: Agent Handoff Between Environments
tips.content: Start a task with a local agent for interactive exploration, then hand it off: switch to Copilot CLI for background execution, or to a Cloud agent to create a pull request. The full conversation history carries over across all agent types.

tips.title: Smart Code Actions
tips.content: Right-click any selection and look for Copilot options in the context menu: 'Explain', 'Fix', 'Generate Tests', and 'Review and Comment'. These smart actions send targeted prompts without opening the full Chat view.

tips.title: Autopilot Permission Level
tips.content: Set the permission level in the Chat view to 'Autopilot (Preview)' to let the agent auto-approve all tool calls, auto-respond to questions, and run until the task is fully complete. Use 'Default Approvals' when you want to review each tool call.

tips.title: Vision: Attach Images as Context
tips.content: Drag and drop a screenshot, UI mockup, or architecture diagram directly into the Chat input. Copilot reads the image and uses it as context — great for 'implement this UI from the mockup' or 'explain what this diagram shows'.

tips.title: Copilot Extensions Marketplace
tips.content: Install Copilot Extensions from the VS Code Marketplace to add domain-specific agents: Docker, Azure, Terraform, GitHub Actions, and more. Extensions register as @ participants so you can invoke them directly in chat (e.g., @docker).

tips.title: Cloud Agent Creates Pull Requests
tips.content: Assign a GitHub issue to Copilot on GitHub.com (or via the GitHub Pull Requests extension in VS Code) and the Cloud agent creates a branch, implements the changes, and opens a PR for your team to review — fully autonomous background work.
